summary: Ezra and Nehemiah is a card-driven tableau and engine-building game from Shem Phillips (of Raiders of the North Sea / Architects of the West Kingdom fame) with a biblical setting, focused on chaining multi-use cards to rebuild Jerusalem's walls and temple. It plays as a mid-heavy Euro with tech-track progression and a strong solo mode, in the vein of his other Garphill Games titles.
praised: High production values and thematic art
Approachable for fans of the designer's other games
criticised: Theme may feel niche or overly specific to some buyers
Can feel like a reskin of familiar Garphill Games mechanisms
Rulebook/iconography learning curve typical of the designer's catalog

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light competition for shared resources
interaction.detail: Each player builds their own tableau and progresses along personal tracks, so most of the game happens on individual boards rather than a shared space. Interaction is limited to competing over shared card offers or race elements rather than direct conflict.

scoring.how_you_win: Over three weeks of daily worker actions you build the Temple, rebuild walls and gates, teach the Torah, and tend the altar and land; after the third Sabbath all VP sources are tallied and whoever has the most wins.
